title: decision: an unfillable gap is not asked about again
description:
INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC. Mark decided 2026-11-25.

## The question

A hub answers 410 when the range asked for is older than it holds
(docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §5.1). Stage C recorded that, but fill_gap
did not read the flag, so the next fill asked again and got 410 again.

## The readings

1. Return at once for a gap already known unfillable, keeping both the
   flag and which sequence is missing. Chosen.
2. Clear gap_from as well: the gap is resolved by giving up, so the room
   is no longer "behind by a known amount".
3. Keep asking.

## Why 1

Retention only ever deletes. A range a hub has dropped cannot come back,
so a repeat request cannot succeed -- not now and not later. Asking
again is a request that is known in advance to fail.

Reading 2 was rejected because which sequence is missing is the useful
part of the record: an operator asking why a room's clients resynced
wants the hole's position, and nothing else keeps it. The room being
permanently "behind by a known amount" is not misleading, it is true.

## Consequences

- Store::follower_position's `unfillable` is read before anything is
  asked, so the flag is load-bearing and not only a diagnostic.
- A hub that restored history from a backup would not be picked up.
  Accepted: that is not a thing retention does.
